title: r/longevity on Reddit: The Sheekey Science Show explores the research behind fisetin, a potential senolytic therapeutic which is undergoing study in humans at the Mayo Clinic.
abstract:
Feeling old mentally happens sadly, no matter age. I'm not sure about long term regular Fisetin though - definitely seems great when used as a strong short dose senolytic as per Mayo Clinic trials i.e.

Although human biology is complex and there are hundreds of age-related pathologies, the geroscience hypothesis proposes that it is possible to delay or prevent the onset of age-related ill health and increase healthy lifespan by targeting the biological mechanisms of aging.
